title: Did Reagan's Star Wars program win the Cold War?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine Ronald Reagan's Strategic Defense Initiative, nicknamed "Star Wars," announced in a March 1983 address to challenge the scientific community to make nuclear weapons "impotent and obsolete." They cover the mutual assured destruction doctrine, Soviet opposition and treaty objections (ABM Treaty, Outer Space Treaty), congressional and public skepticism, the Fletcher Report, the Reykjavik talks with Gorbachev, the Soviet Polyus response, and the program's shrinkage under Bush and Clinton. Technologies discussed include Project Excalibur (X-ray laser, Edward Teller), kinetic warheads and the "garage" concept, rail guns, the MIRACL chemical laser, and Brilliant Pebbles, which was later repurposed for the Clementine moon mapping probe. The episode ends with a listener mail segment answering Facebook questions about recording seats, favorite bands, coffee, and food preferences.

segments.title: Opening banter and housekeeping
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh chat casually, then address newcomers about not claiming to be infallible experts and note that they make research errors from time to time.

segments.title: Mutual assured destruction and Reagan's new plan
segments.summary: The hosts describe mutual assured destruction as the Cold War standoff and say Reagan found it morally and politically distasteful, so he proposed the Strategic Defense Initiative. Reagan's March 3 address challenged scientists to make nuclear weapons impotent and obsolete.
topics: Reagan March address nuclear weapons obsolete

segments.title: Soviet reaction and treaty objections
segments.summary: The Soviets, led by Andropov, opposed the program and ran a propaganda campaign, arguing it could enable a first strike. They said it violated the ABM Treaty and the Outer Space Treaty. Many in Congress and the public were skeptical, and Ted Kennedy is credited with coining the term Star Wars, which Reagan tried unsuccessfully to stop.

segments.title: Skepticism, the Fletcher Report and Reykjavik
segments.summary: Allies and Congress worried about cost and feasibility. The Fletcher Report listed technologies needed for the program. At the Reykjavik meeting, Gorbachev offered arms reductions contingent on abandoning Star Wars, and Reagan refused and walked out.

segments.title: Soviet response, Soviet collapse and later scaling back
segments.summary: The Soviets began the Polyus project to counter the program but lacked funding. The hosts argue the defense spending strained the Soviet economy before its collapse. Bush and Clinton then cut back and refocused the program.
topics: Bush and Clinton scaling back SDI

segments.title: Weaponizing space and the X-ray laser
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the need to place weapons in space to intercept ICBMs and the environmental question of nuclear detonations in space. They cover Edward Teller's X-ray laser concept, Project Excalibur, its failed test and alleged falsified results, and its ridicule in the media.

segments.title: Kinetic warheads, rail guns, MIRACL and Brilliant Pebbles
segments.summary: Other concepts included kinetic warheads from a satellite garage, rail guns, and the ground-based MIRACL chemical laser. The hosts then describe Brilliant Pebbles, its cost, its tests including the Clementine probe, and a computer model of Scud interception. They note the later missile defense system descends from SDI.

segments.title: Legacy and test shootdowns
segments.summary: The hosts say some SDI tests succeeded, and that sensor and other research carried into modern missile defense, including a recent Pearl Harbor test interception.

segments.title: Sponsor read and show promotion
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh point listeners to the How Stuff Works search bar for more Star Wars content, and mention a sponsor read.

segments.title: Listener mail: Facebook questions
segments.summary: The hosts answer listener questions about which recording booth seat they sit in, favorite Marvel hero, favorite band, Margaret Hamilton-style character opinions, speed limit personality, least favorite food, and coffee preferences.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck give contact information for the show on Twitter, Facebook and email and sign off.
